alt.en: A printed title page reading "Thoughts upon the African Slave Trade. By John Newton, Rector of St. Mary Woolnoth", with a verse from Matthew 7:12 and "London: printed for J. Buckland, in Pater-noster-row; and J. Johnson, in St. Paul's Church-yard. M.DCC.LXXXVIII." A past owner has written "No. 4" in ink at the top right.
alt.es: Portada impresa con el texto "Thoughts upon the African Slave Trade. By John Newton, Rector of St. Mary Woolnoth", un versículo de Mateo 7:12 y "London: printed for J. Buckland, in Pater-noster-row; and J. Johnson, in St. Paul's Church-yard. M.DCC.LXXXVIII." Un antiguo dueño escribió "No. 4" a tinta arriba a la derecha.

caption.en: The title page of Newton's Thoughts upon the African Slave Trade (London, 1788), the pamphlet in which the former slave-ship captain made what he called a public confession.
caption.es: Portada de Thoughts upon the African Slave Trade, de Newton (Londres, 1788), el folleto en el que el antiguo capitán de barcos negreros hizo lo que llamó una confesión pública.

source: Thoughts upon the African slave trade, by John Newton (London: printed for J. Buckland and J. Johnson, 1788), title page

alt.en: A colour photograph of a tall stone church tower and spire, with a black clock face and gold numerals on the tower, rising above dark yew trees and gravestones, seen from a lane between a stone wall and an iron gate under a cloudy sky.
alt.es: Fotografía en color de una alta torre de piedra con su aguja, con un reloj de esfera negra y números dorados en la torre, que se alza sobre tejos oscuros y lápidas, vista desde un camino entre un muro de piedra y una verja de hierro bajo un cielo nublado.

caption.en: The spire of Olney's parish church, where Newton was curate from 1764; he wrote Amazing Grace for his parish for New Year's Day 1773.
caption.es: La aguja de la iglesia parroquial de Olney, donde Newton fue coadjutor desde 1764; escribió Amazing Grace para su parroquia, para el día de Año Nuevo de 1773.

source: Spire of Ss Peter and Paul, Olney (photograph, 27 September 2019)
licenceEvidence: The file's own page: source "Own work", licence {{self|cc-zero}}, shown as "Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication" (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). The photographer released his own photograph of the building.

alt.en: A printed book page headed "Hy. 41. I. Chronicles. 53". Hymn XL fills the top half; below a row of small diamond ornaments comes "I. Chronicles. Hymn XLI. Faith's review and expectation. Chap. xvii. 16, 17." and the first verse, "Amazing grace! (how sweet the sound)", set in old type with the long s. There is no music.
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro con el encabezado "Hy. 41. I. Chronicles. 53". El himno XL ocupa la mitad de arriba; bajo una fila de pequeños rombos decorativos aparece "I. Chronicles. Hymn XLI. Faith's review and expectation. Chap. xvii. 16, 17." y la primera estrofa, "Amazing grace! (how sweet the sound)", en tipografía antigua con la s larga. No hay música.

caption.en: Newton's first verse as printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, No. 41, under the title "Faith's review and expectation" and with no tune.
caption.es: La primera estrofa de Newton tal como se imprimió en Olney Hymns (Londres, 1779), libro I, n.º 41, con el título "Faith's review and expectation" (la fe mira atrás y espera) y sin melodía.

source: Olney Hymns, in Three Books, by John Newton and William Cowper (London: W. Oliver, 1779), Book I, Hymn XLI, p. 53
library: Internet Archive, Eighteenth Century collection (from microfilm)
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1779; authors John Newton died 1807 and William Cowper died 1800. Faithful microfilm scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).

alt.en: A yellowed page of music headed "8", "NEW BRITAIN. C. M." and "Baptist Harmony, p. 123." Three staves in 3/4 time use notes with differently shaped heads: squares, triangles, ovals and diamonds. Verse 1, "Amazing grace! (how sweet the sound)", runs under the top staff, verse 2 under the second, and verses 3 to 6 are printed in four columns below.
alt.es: Página amarillenta de música con el encabezado "8", "NEW BRITAIN. C. M." y "Baptist Harmony, p. 123." Tres pentagramas en 3/4 llevan notas con cabezas de formas distintas: cuadrados, triángulos, óvalos y rombos. La estrofa 1, "Amazing grace! (how sweet the sound)", va bajo el pentagrama de arriba, la estrofa 2 bajo el segundo, y las estrofas 3 a 6 están impresas debajo en cuatro columnas.

caption.en: NEW BRITAIN with Newton's words on page 8 of William Walker's The Southern Harmony (1835), in shape notes: the earliest known pairing of the hymn and the tune we sing.
caption.es: NEW BRITAIN con la letra de Newton en la página 8 de The Southern Harmony, de William Walker (1835), en notación de formas: la primera unión conocida del himno y la melodía que cantamos.

source: The Southern Harmony, and Musical Companion, by William Walker (Spartanburg, S.C.: sold by the author, 1835), p. 8, "New Britain. C. M."
library: Oberlin College Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published 1835; compiler William Walker 1809-1875; Newton died 1807; the tune's maker is unknown and its earliest known printing is 1829. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
